title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
Problem: integrate dx/√X = dy/√Y with X = A+Bx+Cx², Y = A+By+Cy². This is the degenerate quadratic case of the Fagnano–Euler addition problem, worked by Lagrange's method.

On the previous page Euler introduces an auxiliary variable t with dx/dt = √X and dy/dt = √Y. Differentiating the squares gives 2x'' = X' and 2y''= Y'. For p = x+y this yields 2p'' = 2B + 2Cp. Multiplying by p' and integrating gives p'² = Δ + 2Bp + Cp², with Δ the constant of integration.

On this page, since p' = √X + √Y, he obtains the algebraic integral √X + √Y = √(Δ + 2B(x+y) + C(x+y)²).

§29: Squaring gives 2A + B(x+y) + C(x²+y²) + 2√(XY) = Δ + 2B(x+y) + C(x+y)². Equivalently, 2√(XY) = Γ + B(x+y) + 2Cxy, where Γ = Δ − 2A. Squaring again removes the radical. Collecting terms gives the rational relation
(4A²−Γ²) + 2B(2A−Γ)(x+y) + 4(B²−ΓC)xy + 4AC(x²+y²) − B²(x+y)² = 0.

§30: Expanding (x+y)² and comparing with Euler's own 'canonical' symmetric relation α + 2β(x+y) + γ(x²+y²) + 2δxy = 0 gives
α = 4A²−Γ², β = B(2A−Γ), γ = 4AC−B², δ = B²−2ΓC.

The point is that Lagrange's dynamical trick reproduces exactly the symmetric biquadratic (here biquadratic of degree 2) integral that Euler had earlier obtained by his own methods. It also shows that the constant Γ is the parameter of the addition law. In modern terms this is the addition theorem for arcsin/arcsinh/log-type integrals of 1/√(quadratic).
errors: None in the mathematics on this page; all expansions and coefficient identifications check out (e.g. xy coefficient 4B²−4ΓC−2B² = 2(B²−2ΓC) gives δ = B²−2ΓC).

ideas.what: Lagrange's method: introduce an auxiliary 'time' t, form second-order equations, and integrate the sum p = x+y after multiplying by dp, obtaining an algebraic integral of dx/√X = dy/√Y.
ideas.modern_name: Lagrange's dynamical/energy-integral proof of the Euler addition theorem
ideas.where_published: E506 itself (Acta Acad. Sci. Imp. Petrop. 1778 [1780] II:1)

ideas.what: Rationalized integral written as a symmetric relation of degree 2 in each variable: α + 2β(x+y) + γ(x²+y²) + 2δxy = 0.
ideas.modern_name: Symmetric biquadratic (Euler) relation / algebraic addition law for the integral of 1/√(quadratic)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (1750s papers on elliptic integrals; Institutiones calculi integralis I)
ideas.where_published: Euler's papers on comparison of elliptic arcs (e.g. E251, E261) and Institutiones calculi integralis vol. I (E342); exact chapter unsure

ideas.what: Explicit dictionary between the integration constant Γ = Δ−2A and the canonical coefficients α, β, γ, δ.
ideas.modern_name: Parametrization of the addition correspondence by the integration constant

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct, routine algebraic verification that Lagrange's method reproduces Euler's known canonical symmetric relation in the elementary quadratic case. It is well documented in the history of elliptic integrals and contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The page transcription matches the image well. Δ (printed as a small triangle) is the integration constant and Γ = Δ − 2A as printed.
In §29 the image line reads '2A − B(x+y) − 2Cxy + 2√XY = Δ', consistent with the transcription.
